newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil down at close on unexciting export.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil down at close on unexciting export.

text.p: PALM OIL FUTURES PALM OIL PHYSICAL

PALM OIL FUTURES - Lower after export figures released by SGS (M) Sdn Bhd and Caleb Brett came within market expectations and prompted profit-taking. Technical selling also evident among players who saw the market as having hit a high. Near-term support at 1,210 while resistance at 1,235.
PALM OIL PHYSICALS - Quiet, with little volatility seen.
"There was profit-taking after that, as there were no other leads," he added.
Another trader said the market was thought to have hit its peak by some players, leading to technical selling.
"The general idea was that it had reached its top-range," said one trader, explaining the fall in August third-month futures after it hit a high of 1,234 ringgit.
At the close, the contract ended 11 ringgit lower at 1,219 ringgit ($484.69) a tonne. Double-digit losses were also seen in other contracts.
Traders saw August trading at between 1,215 and 1,235 in the near-term.
Volume on futures market was at 1,484 lots.
The physicals market was quiet and lacked volatility.
Physical June (south) saw offers at 1,275 against bids at 1,272.50 with earlier trades done at 1,280 and 1,275.
June (central) saw offers at 1,267.50 after bids at 1,260.
July (south) saw offers at 1,270 after bids of 1,262.50 and trade of 1,270 and 1,265.
